questions.stem: Why do red blood cells have no nucleus?

options.text: So they can divide more quickly to replace old cells
So there is more space inside the cell to pack in haemoglobin
So they can change shape to fight infections
So they can produce antibodies more efficiently

questions.explanation: Red blood cells lose their nucleus during development. This frees up space inside the cell to carry more haemoglobin, maximising the amount of oxygen each cell can transport.
